speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash, low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; please tell me, when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

The timeline of prodromal symptoms (fever, rhinorrhea, headache) followed by a rash that started on the face and spread downward while sparing the perioral area is classic for measles. I would like to confirm if the patient has been vaccinated with the MMR vaccine and if anyone around her has had recent contact with a confirmed case.
